exact_claim_or_summary: Analysis of NCHS U.S. annual birth volumes (1909–2018) identifies a single sharp structural discontinuity at the 1946 post-war baby boom (+19.3% YoY to 3.411M births), whereas Strauss-Howe turning transitions (1901, 1924, 1960/64, 1982, 2008) show no statistically significant breaks in birth numbers or General Fertility Rate.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) vital statistics 1909–2018; scripts/step13_demography_check.py
important_assumptions: NCHS birth registration completeness and standard vital statistics reporting conventions
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Generational theorists argue cohort peer personalities are defined by childhood social mood rather than birth count inflections
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (direct federal vital statistics time series)

exact_claim_or_summary: The Strauss-Howe generational chronology exhibits substantial internal duration variability across its five completed saecula, ranging from 71 to 110 years (mean 91.8, standard deviation 16.7), with Crisis turnings ranging from 5 to 29 years.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Strauss & Howe (1991; 1997) published chronologies; independent tabulation in Neutral Analyses Deep Dive
important_assumptions: Tabulated turning dates represent authors' own formal historical periodization
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Authors argue saeculum durations are elastic distributions governed by biological human lifecycles rather than rigid astronomical periodicity
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (computed directly from authors' published period dates)

exact_claim_or_summary: Longitudinal survey data from the Pew Research Center and National Election Studies (1958–2025) reveal trust in the U.S. federal government fell from 77% in 1964 to 17% in September 2025, with no institutional trust rebuilding observed during the claimed Millennial Crisis (2008–2025).
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Pew Research Center Public Trust in Government 1958–2025 series (Sept 2025 release)
important_assumptions: Representative national probability sampling methodologies across survey waves
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Strauss-Howe model predicts civic cohesion and institutional trust rebuild during the climax of a Fourth Turning rather than early or mid-phase
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (official Pew Research Center benchmark polling panels)

exact_claim_or_summary: Independent consensus reviews by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (2020) and Pew Research Center (2023) conclude that popular generational labels lack empirical validity in workforce and attitudinal research due to the Age-Period-Cohort identification problem.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: NASEM (2020) workforce consensus report; Pew Research Center (2023) Decoded methodology series
important_assumptions: Linear dependency of Age = Period - Cohort precludes unique non-parametric econometric identification
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Qualitative sociological researchers argue generational archetypes serve as useful macro-cultural heuristics even if statistically confounded
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (peer-reviewed demographic and institutional consensus reports)

exact_claim_or_summary: Historical case studies of major technological installation waves (1840s British Railway Mania, 1929 stock market crash, and 2000 dot-com bubble) demonstrate long empirical gestation lags of 18 to 37 years between foundational innovation breakthroughs and peak financial frenzy.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Odlyzko (2010); Perez (2002, 2009); Federal Reserve historical monetary data; NBER business cycle chronologies
important_assumptions: Techno-economic surge periodization from foundational 'big bang' innovations to financial decoupling
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Standard neoclassical macroeconomics views speculative bubbles as idiosyncratic asset-market shocks rather than regular long-wave cycle stages
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (documented financial and infrastructure historical time series)

exact_claim_or_summary: Empirical econometric testing of long-wave theories demonstrates that 45-to-60-year cyclical waves are prominent in pre-1945 wholesale and commodity price series, but statistically disputed in real output (GDP) series due to the Slutsky-Yule moving-average filtering effect.
important_assumptions: De-trending methodology and spectral estimation specifications on historical GDP time series
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Korotayev and Tsirel (2010) report spectral peaks in world GDP growth rates at p~0.04-0.05, though based on fewer than three complete cycles
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate-to-High (broad econometric consensus on price vs real output wave visibility)

exact_claim_or_summary: Major long-wave historiographical frameworks (Kondratiev, Schumpeter, Perez, Smihula, Nefiodow) disagree substantially on cycle dating and phase boundaries, with proposed onset dates for the modern 'sixth wave' ranging from 1971 to 2020.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Comparative historiographical synthesis across Kondratiev (1925), Schumpeter (1939), Perez (2002), Smihula (2011), and Nefiodow (2014)
important_assumptions: Literature definitions of techno-economic paradigms and installation versus deployment phases
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Long-wave proponents argue variation reflects differing national diffusion lags across core vs peripheral economies
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (direct comparison of published academic chronologies)

exact_claim_or_summary: Real-time recognition of macroeconomic cycle turning points is consistently impaired by measurement and decision lags, as demonstrated by the NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee establishing peak dates 6 to 12 months after occurrences and historical authorities misidentifying structural inflections in real time.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: NBER Business Cycle Dating announcements; Federal Reserve historical transcripts (1929; 1996; 2007–2008)
important_assumptions: Revisions in real-time GDP and payroll telemetry relative to finalized benchmark revisions
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: High-frequency nowcasting and financial yield-curve spreads provide earlier probabilistic signals of recession turning points
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (official NBER and Federal Reserve historical records)

exact_claim_or_summary: Quantitative text-based sentiment indices, including the Baker-Bloom-Davis Economic Policy Uncertainty index (1985–2025) and narrative economic studies (Shiller 2017, Tetlock 2007), capture acute short-to-medium-term business cycle shocks but show no evidence of an autonomous 40-to-60-year long-wave sentiment cycle.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Baker, Bloom, & Davis (2016) EPU index dataset; Tetlock (2007); Shiller (2017)
important_assumptions: Newspaper textual coverage frequency serves as an accurate proxy for public and market sentiment
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Long-wave cultural theorists argue generational forgetting occurs over 50-year spans without leaving distinct continuous text index signatures
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (corroborated across continuous newspaper text indices)

exact_claim_or_summary: While Landauer's thermodynamic bound (2.87e-21 J/bit at 300 K) has been confirmed experimentally, current frontier supercomputers (June 2025 Green500 JEDI at 72.73 GFLOPS/W) operate roughly 5 billion times above the Landauer limit per 64-bit operation, demonstrating that thermodynamic bounds do not constrain 2026–2035 computing.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Landauer (1961); Bérut et al. (2012 Nature); Green500 June 2025 official list
important_assumptions: Bit erasure count per 64-bit double-precision floating-point operation on contemporary CMOS hardware
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: At room temperature, interconnect thermal dissipation and power delivery walls create practical engineering limits well before Landauer dissipation is reached
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (exact physical arithmetic and experimental validation)

exact_claim_or_summary: Bloom, Jones, Van Reenen, and Webb (2020) demonstrate that the number of researchers required to sustain Moore's Law doubling of semiconductor chip density has increased by more than a factor of 18 since 1970, showing that exponential progress in computing is driven by exponentially rising inputs.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Bloom, Jones, Van Reenen, & Webb (2020 AER); Semiconductor Industry Association historical R&D data
important_assumptions: Deflated corporate and industry R&D expenditure tracks effective researcher labour inputs
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Proponents of AI-augmented discovery argue AI research assistants will decouple effective research effort from human population constraints
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (peer-reviewed empirical econometrics across multiple micro-datasets)

exact_claim_or_summary: Empirical AI training compute grew 4-5x annually from 2010 to 2024, with training runs of 2e29 FLOP projected by Epoch AI as feasible by 2030, while U.S. data-center electricity consumption is projected by LBNL to rise from 176 TWh (4.4% of U.S. electricity) in 2023 to 325–580 TWh (6.7–12%) by 2028.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Epoch AI (May/Aug 2024 studies); Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Jan 2025 report); IEA (April 2025 Energy & AI)
important_assumptions: Datacenter power buildouts, semiconductor manufacturing capacity, and sustained capital returns on frontier AI training
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Grid interconnect bottlenecks, model efficiency gains (quantization, distillation), or disappointing commercial returns could force earlier plateauing
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate-to-High (consensus projections from official laboratory and research bodies)

exact_claim_or_summary: Empirical testing of Kurzweil's Law of Accelerating Returns against macroeconomic endogenous growth models (Solow 1957, Romer 1990, Jones 1995) using BLS nonfarm output-per-hour (1948–2025) shows U.S. labor productivity grew at an average of 2.1% annually, decelerating to ~1.5% after 2005, showing no evidence of economy-wide growth takeoff.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: BLS Series OPHNFB (1948–2025); scripts/step13_productivity_check.py; Nordhaus (2021 AEJ:Macro)
important_assumptions: Standard BLS nonfarm business sector productivity measurement methodology and GDP price deflators
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Some digital economists argue GDP mismeasures free digital goods and that AI deployment lags mean productivity gains will appear with a multi-year delay
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (official Bureau of Labor Statistics 77-year empirical time series)

exact_claim_or_summary: Sevilla et al. (2022) identify three distinct empirical regimes in machine learning training compute: the Pre-Deep Learning era (1952–2010, doubling every 17–29 months), the Deep Learning era (2010–2015, doubling every 5–6 months), and the Large-Scale era (2015–2024+, doubling every 3.4–4.0 months), driven by specialized hardware and capital concentration.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Sevilla et al. (2022 IEEE/arXiv); Epoch AI empirical compute dataset
important_assumptions: Milestone selection criteria and estimated FLOP totals for published historical systems
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Capital expenditure scaling per training run accounted for the majority of the post-2015 acceleration rather than fundamental silicon physics
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (standardized empirical benchmark across >800 machine learning models)

exact_claim_or_summary: Empirical research by Erdil and Besiroglu (2022, 2023) demonstrates that algorithmic efficiency in deep learning halved the compute required to achieve fixed benchmark performance roughly every 8 to 9 months in vision and language modeling between 2012 and 2023.
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Erdil & Besiroglu (2022; 2023 Epoch AI reports on vision and language algorithmic progress)
important_assumptions: Standard benchmark metrics (ImageNet top-1 accuracy; language model perplexity) accurately capture algorithmic efficiency gains
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Algorithmic progress may saturate as architectures encounter task-specific diminishing returns or data bottlenecks
confidence_and_uncertainty: High (empirical econometric analysis of machine learning benchmarks)

exact_claim_or_summary: Pew Research Center national panels (2021–2023) show U.S. public sentiment toward artificial intelligence shifted from 37% more concerned than excited in 2021 to 52% in August 2023, with concern shared equally across political parties (54% Republican vs 52% Democrat).
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Pew Research Center (August & November 2023 national survey reports)
important_assumptions: Probability-based American Trends Panel methodology with demographic weighting
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Public attitudes may fluctuate rapidly as consumer-facing applications demonstrate tangible personal utility

exact_claim_or_summary: Cross-national surveys by Reuters Institute (2024) across six nations and Stanford HAI / Ipsos (2023–2024) across 31 countries show low daily generative AI usage (2% to 7%) and a stark geographic divide: Western publics report low optimism (35% in the U.S. seeing net benefits), whereas emerging economies report high optimism (78% in China, 69% in Indonesia).
supporting_evidence_and_sources: Fletcher et al. (2024 Reuters Institute); Stanford HAI AI Index (2024); Ipsos (2023)
important_assumptions: Standard online and quota sampling methodologies across international survey jurisdictions
counterevidence_or_competing_explanation: Online survey panels in developing nations may over-sample urban, higher-income, and tech-literate populations
